correctness.rationale: Every deck group element is classified as even/odd glide, giving the exact two-candidate quotient distance. For a >= b/2 the vertical square difference stays inside the uniform horizontal-deck interval; exact positive-part integration gives the fixed-anchor correction. The circular autocorrelation is a polynomial identity checked symbolically and proved by splitting its two integration intervals. Uniform fractional anchors yield exact beta(3,3) and beta(5,5) integrals, proving the covariance b^8/(302400 a^4). The pairwise sample variance follows by exact overlap counting, and the Gaussian limit follows from the bounded nondegenerate order-two Hoeffding projection. Boundary a=b/2 is included. Independent numerical deck-lift quadrature corroborates, rather than replaces, the proof.

value.rationale: The exact nonconstant squared-distance energy detects the nonhomogeneous geometry of a natural one-parameter family of flat nonorientable surfaces. Its sharp anchor extrema and positive three-point covariance distinguish them from homogeneous flat tori, while the area-normalized covariance identifies the aspect ratio exactly. The same invariant supplies the explicit leading sampling variance of all-pairs geodesic dispersion statistics; it is not a mere second calculation of the known one-pair mean. The sharp a >= b/2 domain is the natural threshold at which the deck-penalty integral becomes a single polynomial branch.
